description: Callisto sits outside the Laplace resonance that drives the tidal heating in Io, Europa, and Ganymede — so its interior never melted enough to differentiate fully or resurface its crust. The result is the most pristine record of impact bombardment in the inner Galilean system, including the spectacular Valhalla basin's 15-ring system stretching nearly half the moon's circumference. Despite the lack of tidal heating, Galileo's magnetometer detected an induced magnetic field consistent with a deep salty ocean ~100 km below the surface. Its low radiation environment (compared to Europa or Ganymede) and long-lived water make it a likely staging point for future crewed missions to the Jupiter system.
surface_composition: Roughly 40% water ice + 60% silicate rock; surface the most heavily-cratered in the solar system — almost saturated, untouched by resurfacing. Notable feature: the 3,800 km Valhalla multi-ring impact basin.
mission_visits: Galileo orbiter — USA, 1995–2003 (multiple flybys; ocean candidate)

science_sections.why: Callisto orbits outside the Laplace resonance — its 1.88-million-km semi-major axis puts it beyond the worst of Jupiter's radiation belts, making it the most spacecraft-friendly Galilean.
Callisto's 0.007 eccentricity is small and unforced — without resonant pumping, no tidal flexing, no subsurface ocean (probably).
